target_customer: Startups and mid-size businesses (under about 1,000 employees) that reimburse employee expenses and reconcile corporate cards
problem: Month-end expense reports are slow and painful for employees and finance teams. Abacus let employees submit expenses in real time from a phone and triggered reimbursement once approved.
business_model: B2B SaaS per active user (about $5 per active user per month at the 2014 funding announcement)

founders.name: Omar Qari
founders.background_notes: No background listed on the YC page or in the sources opened.

founders.name: Joshua Halickman
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder/CTO on the YC page; no background listed.

founders.name: Ted Power
founders.background_notes: Employers per the YC page. Built In NYC says he wanted a product as simple as Venmo, which he saw at his previous job. Later co-founded Versa (S22).

competitors.name: Concur
competitors.what: Incumbent travel and expense report software owned by SAP

competitors.name: Expensify
competitors.what: Mobile expense reporting app with receipt scanning

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile apps plus real-time reimbursement and card reconciliation with accounting syncs required payments and integration work, but nothing research-grade.

defensibility.rationale: Accounting integrations and policy rules create some lock-in, but incumbents and Expensify offered overlapping features and the product was easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not buy it. Certify, a mid-market expense vendor, acquired the team and product in July 2018 and kept the Abacus product running; it later became Emburse Spend.

market_need_then: Expense reports were a widely disliked monthly chore. The 2014 round closed in about a week after YC, and Abacus had over 50 customers and early revenue at that point.

branding.domain_note: The team first used abac.us, which took a lot of explaining, then obtained abacus.com when its owner, the Royal Bank of Canada, wanted to unload it just as they were starting (Built In NYC).

identity.voice_and_tone: Quirky, friendly culture; engineers write human-readable code with humor (Built In NYC)

rebrands.why: Emburse unified its brands; one source dates the change to April 2025

brand_strength.rationale: A generic real-word name on an exact-match .com that helped credibility, but no press about the brand itself, mascot or community was found.

outcome_analysis: Abacus launched in 2013, went through YC in Winter 2014, and raised a $3.5M seed in November 2014 from top-tier leads after a fast close. It reached about 1,000 customers including Betterment and Dropbox but stayed small against Concur and Expensify, and was acquired by Certify in July 2018 on undisclosed terms. The outcome looks like a modest strategic exit for a product with traction that did not reach escape velocity.
notes: Only the 2014 seed is confirmed; no later rounds found, so coverage is partial. Total raised is not stated in sources opened. An aggregator mention of a $4M Abacus Labs seed in October 2014 is unverified and possibly a different entity. The abacus.com site now redirects to Emburse Spend. The competitor entries rely on the search result summary of the February 2014 TechCrunch article, which was not opened directly.
